Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:1.hebrew: ואחזוק ולא אחזוק בדלא כתיבא תנאי היא - מצוה שאינה כתובה בפירוש בתורה וראינו שהחזיקו בה, אי אמרינן כיון דאחזוק לדידהו אחזוק נמי לדידן לסמוך עלייהו כי עבדי לצורך עצמן, או אי אמרינן אע"ג דאחזוק לדידהו לא אחזוק לדידן, כלומר לא חשבינן ליה חזקה למסמך עלייהו, תנאי פליגי בה. אחזוק ולא אחזוק, כלומר חזקה או אינה חזקה:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:1.english: "Established practice or no established practice" in the case of something not written [in the Torah] is a Tannaitic dispute - A commandment that is not written explicitly in the Torah, and we have seen that they [the Samaritans] maintained it as an established practice - [the question is] whether we say that since it is an established practice for them, it is also an established practice for us, so that we may rely on them when they act for their own needs; or whether we say that even though it is an established practice for them, it is not an established practice for us - meaning, we do not consider it a sufficient established practice to rely on them - this is a matter of Tannaitic dispute. "Established practice or no established practice" means: is it a valid established practice or not.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:2.hebrew: מותר - לאוכלה, ולא חיישינן לחמץ בפסח:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:2.english: It is permitted - to eat it, and we are not concerned about [it containing] chametz on Passover.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:3.hebrew: ואדם יוצא ידי חובתו - שהכתוב קבעו חובה לאכול מצה בלילה ראשונה, דכתיב (שמות י״ב:י״ח) בערב תאכלו מצות, ואם ישב ולא אכל עבר בעשה. ולקמן פריך: כיון דתנא מותר, פשיטא דיוצא בה:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:11:3.english: And a person fulfills his obligation with it - For Scripture established it as an obligation to eat matzah on the first night, as it is written (Exodus 12:18): "In the evening you shall eat unleavened bread," and if one sat and did not eat, he transgressed a positive commandment. And further on [the Gemara] asks: since it was taught that it is permitted, isn't it obvious that one fulfills his obligation with it?

Rashi on Chullin 4a:1:1.english: A string [dekurya] - Strings of slaughtered birds. Reisht, in Old French.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:2:1.hebrew: אביי - דאמר לעיל: יוצא ונכנס לכתחלה לא שרינן גבי שחיטה, דייק מרישא:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:2:1.english: Abaye - [This refers to] what he said above: we do not permit, ab initio, [relying on] intermittently going out and coming in with regard to slaughter [as sufficient supervision]. He derives this precisely from the first clause [of the mishna].

Rashi on Chullin 4a:2:2.hebrew: ורבא - דשרי, דייק מסיפא דלא מצריך תנא בדיקה אלא היכא דבא ומצאו:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:2:2.english: And Rava - who permits [in the case where the Jew exits and enters], infers from the latter clause that the Tanna requires examination [i.e., feeding the Samaritan a piece of the slaughtered animal] only in a case where he came and found that he had [already] slaughtered.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:4:1.hebrew: כעומד על גביו דמי - ועומד על גביו דקתני תנא, היינו יוצא ונכנס:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:4:1.english: It is considered like standing over it - [The phrase] "standing over it," which the tanna teaches, that is [equivalent to a case of] one who exits and enters.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:5:1.hebrew: האי הוא דהוי שחיט שפיר - אותו עוף לבדו שחוט יפה, וזה היה מכירו ואכלו, ואנן היכי נסמוך לאכול האחרים:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:5:1.english: Perhaps it is this one that was properly slaughtered - [Perhaps] only that bird was properly slaughtered, and this [Samaritan] recognized it and ate it, but how can we rely [on that] to eat the rest?

Rashi on Chullin 4a:6:1.hebrew: במכניסן תחת כנפיו - ישראל זה הבודקו, מכניס כל הצפרים תחת כנפי כסותו, ואין הכותי מכיר איזה נתן לו:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:6:1.english: By bringing them in under his wings [i.e., garment] - This Israelite who examines him [the Samaritan] brings all the birds in under the wings of his garment, so that the Samaritan (Kuthite) cannot tell which one was given to him.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:7:1.english: He crushed [it] - He squeezed it and pounded it.

Rashi on Chullin 4a:8:1.hebrew: אין שחיטה לעוף מן התורה - משום דלא כתיב זביחה בהדיא אלא בבקר וצאן, דכתיב וזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך, ואנן ילפינן בהקישא לקמן (חולין דף כז:) מזאת תורת הבהמה והעוף:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:8:1.english: There is no [Biblically mandated] slaughter for a bird - because [the term] "slaughter" is not written explicitly except regarding cattle and flock, as it is written, "and you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your flock," and we derive it below (Chullin 27b) by way of an analogy from "this is the law of the animal and the bird."

Rashi on Chullin 4a:9:1.hebrew: ולטעמיך - הך זביחה דכתיב בבקר ובצאן, מי מפרשן הלכותיה בתורה? ואפ"ה סמכי עלייהו, משום דאחזיק להו דאחזיקו בה:
Rashi on Chullin 4a:9:1.english: And according to your reasoning - This [very act of] slaughter, which is written [as done] on cattle and on flock - are its halachot spelled out in the Torah? Yet even so we rely upon them, because it has become an established practice, in that they have held fast to it.

Tosafot on Chullin 4a:11:1.hebrew: מצת כותי מותרת - וא"ת: והלא גזרו על פתן, לפי שהיו מבטלין בנין בית המקדש בימי עזרא, כדאמר בפירקין דר"א (פ' לח)? וליכא למימר דהיינו בכותים ראשונים, דכתיב בהם "ואת אלהיהם היו עובדים", דהא קאמר התם: מכאן אמר ר"א, כל האוכל פת כותי כאילו אוכל בשר חזיר. ותנינא נמי לקמן (חולין דף יג.): שחיטת צדוקי לעבודת כוכבים, פתו פת כותי. ואומר ר"ת דמיירי הכא בעיסה דישראל שעשה הכותי ממנה מצה. וא"ת: והיאך יוצא בה, ושמא הוא לא שמר לשם מצה, דהא חשידי אלפני עור לא תתן מכשול? וי"ל כגון שלא אכל הכותי מצה אחרת כל הלילה:
Tosafot on Chullin 4a:11:1.english: The matzah of a Samaritan (Kuthi) is permitted - And if you say: but did they not decree against their bread, because they used to hinder the building of the Beit HaMikdash in the days of Ezra, as is stated in Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer (ch. 38)? And one cannot say that this [decree] refers to the original Samaritans (Kuthim Rishonim), about whom it is written, "and they would worship their gods" - for it states there: from this [incident], Rabbi Eliezer said, anyone who eats the bread of a Samaritan is as if he ate pig meat. And we have also learned further on (Chullin 13a): the slaughter of a Sadducee (Tzeduki) is [treated] as if for idol worship, [and] his bread is [treated] as the bread of a Samaritan. And Rabbeinu Tam says that here we are dealing with dough belonging to a Jew, from which a Samaritan made matzah. And if you say: but how does one fulfill his obligation with it - perhaps he did not guard it for the sake of matzah, since they [Samaritans] are suspect of [transgressing] "you shall not place a stumbling block before the blind"? We can answer: [this works in] a case where the Samaritan ate no other matzah the entire night.

Tosafot on Chullin 4a:1:1.hebrew: דקוריא - סל, כמו דקוריא דפרק השוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ דף פד.), ודמפנין (שבת קכז.):
Tosafot on Chullin 4a:1:1.english: Dekurya - A basket, like [the word] "dekurya" [used] in the chapter "HaSocher Et HaPoalim" (Bava Metzia 84a), and in [the chapter dealing with] "clearing out" (Shabbat 127a).

Tosafot on Chullin 4a:6:1.hebrew: מכניס איזמל בזכרים - סימני שמעתתא דרב מנשה, דהא מכילתא הן: הך ד"מכניס תחת כנפיו", ולקמן בפרק שני (חולין דף לא.) "איזמל שאין לו קרנים", ובפרק אלו טרפות (לקמן חולין דף נא.) "הנהו דיכרי דגנבי גנבי, אין חוששין לריסוק אברים". מיהו גם במקומות אחרים יש, כדאשכחנא בפרק ב' דיבמות (דף כה.) דאמר רב מנשה: גזלן דדבריהם כשר לעדות אשה, ובפרק מי שהחשיך (שבת קנו.) אמר רב מנשה: חדא קמי חדא, תרי קמי תרי, שפיר דמי:
Tosafot on Chullin 4a:6:1.english: Inserts a knife, among males - These are the mnemonic markers (simanim) for the teachings (shema'ata) of Rav Menashe, for these are indeed separate teachings: this one, of "inserting [the hand] under its wings" [in our sugya]; and further on, in the second chapter (Chullin 31a), "a slaughtering knife that has no protruding points (keranim)"; and in the chapter "Eilu Treifot" (below, Chullin 51a), "those rams that thieves stole - we do not suspect that their limbs were crushed." However, there are also [teachings of Rav Menashe] in other places, as we find in the second chapter of Yevamot (25a), where Rav Menashe says: a robber [disqualified] only by rabbinic law is valid to testify on behalf of a woman [regarding her husband's death, to permit her to remarry]. And in the chapter "Mi SheHechshich" (Shabbat 156a), Rav Menashe said: one facing one, two facing two, is fine.
